lines: The old oak? (Mr. Page's eyebrows shoot right up.) Funny you should ask. Wait right there.
(He climbs a wobbly ladder to the very top shelf, and comes down with a dusty green book: THE LEGEND OF THE OLD OAK.)
(He reads aloud.) 'Long ago, the oak was planted where two worlds touch. At midnight it hums, and for the chosen ones it opens a door.'
'Wake it with three acorns of light, laid in its roots at sundown. The chosen will know them: they glow, and they tick.'
Fiction, of course. Of course! ...Though I did see something glowing up by Mossy Falls on my morning walk.
Keep it as long as you like. Theo's had the rest of the shop out on loan for years. (He winks.)
'Three acorns of light, laid in its roots at sundown.' I've read it a hundred times. Never once found an acorn that glows.
Welcome to Turn the Page. I'm Lionel Page. Yes, really. With a name like that, what else could I do?
I'm here for the lanterns. Every year I write a wish on mine. Every year it's 'more bookshelves'.
Don't tell anyone, but I came for the gingerbread.
